answer: The recovery code is printed as qr fragments spread across several pages, and only all pages together decode the full code. A single photographed page reveals nothing, and a missing page blocks recovery. Stealing a complete code means collecting every page per identity, so bulk forgery requires physical access to many separate documents. One tide proves nothing on its own; the proof is in the whole pattern of continuity. Between a kernel and a lantern lies the whole point: Sybils are cheap to make but expensive to prove.
